log.title: Write it down once
log.body: Every job, every part, every receipt, attached to the vehicle it belongs to. This is the free half of RigLog, and it is the half you will use every week.

pro.title: When one vehicle isn’t enough
pro.body: Personal opens the garage to more vehicles, and adds the parts that answer questions about the log rather than adding to it — where the money went, who else can see it, and what the whole thing looks like to somebody else.

community.title: Show it, or don’t
community.body: Nothing you write is public until you say so. When you do, a build gets an address of its own that anyone can read without an account.

app.title: Small things that add up
app.body: RigLog is a web app that installs like a native one, speaks Romanian and English, and hands your data back whenever you ask for it.

modes.title: Three modes, one app
modes.body: An off-road build, a restoration and a daily driver need different words for the same screens. You pick the mode when you add a vehicle, and the categories, the status tags and the photo labels change with it. Try it — the preview is the real vocabulary.

tasks.title: Jobs, with what they cost
tasks.body: A job has a name, a category, a status, and what you paid for parts and labour. The cost lives on the work rather than in a spreadsheet beside it, which is the only way it stays accurate.

photos.title: Before, install, after
photos.body: Photos attach to the job they belong to and carry a label, so a year later you can still find the shot of the bracket taken before you cut it. They are resized in the browser first, so a phone photo doesn’t cost you a minute.

documents.title: Documents that remind you
documents.body: Keep the ITP, the insurance and the rest with their expiry dates. RigLog emails you 30 days out, again at 14 and again at 3 — once each, not once per check.

costs.title: What it has cost so far
costs.body: Parts and labour add up per job, per category and per vehicle. A free account sees the running total; Personal sees how it got there.

wishlist.title: The parts you still need
wishlist.body: Keep the list of what you are hunting, with a status from researching to ordered. Mark one as fitted and it becomes a job on the vehicle, with its price already attached.

foundState.title: How you found it
foundState.body: A restoration starts with an honest record of what you bought: the rust, the missing trim, the box of parts in the boot. It never changes afterwards, which is what makes the after photos worth anything.

jobReport.title: A report for the next owner
jobReport.body: Any single job exports as a PDF with its photos, costs and dates — for a warranty claim, a buyer, or the workshop that did the work. Free on every account.

analytics.title: Where the money went
analytics.body: Spend by category, by month, and across any date range you pick, for one vehicle or the whole garage. It is usually the thing that tells you the build cost more in tyres than in suspension.

collaborators.title: Let the mechanic in
collaborators.body: Invite a workshop or a friend to a single vehicle. They can add the jobs they did and nothing else — and one toggle hides every price from them, which matters when the person adding the job is also the person charging for it.

trailLog.title: Where you took it
trailLog.body: Record the track from your phone, drop waypoints with a note and a photo, and keep the run beside the build it belongs to. The map is OpenStreetMap, and recording runs while the screen is on.

cards.title: A card worth posting
cards.body: One button turns a build into a PNG sized for a phone screen — the vehicle, the numbers, and for a restoration the before and after side by side.

limits.title: As many vehicles as you have
limits.body: A free account covers {vehicles, plural, one {one vehicle} other {# vehicles}} and {photos} photos per job. Personal raises both — which is the point at which a garage with a project and a daily driver stops being two accounts.

pdfExport.title: The whole history as a PDF
pdfExport.body: Every job, cost and photo in one document, laid out to be read rather than dumped. Print it for the file, or hand it over with the keys.

originality.title: How original it still is
originality.body: Mark each finished job as OEM, reproduction or modified, and the score follows: the share of the car that is still factory. Buyers and concours judges ask; this answers.

vinDecoder.title: What the chassis number says
vinDecoder.body: Decodes the VIN into year, plant and model where it can — Dacia and Renault Romania from a local table, the rest through the free NHTSA database — and lets you fill it in by hand where it can’t.

priceAlert.title: Tell me when it drops
priceAlert.body: Log the price every time you find the part, set the one you would actually pay, and RigLog emails you the first time a logged price reaches it. Nothing is scraped — you enter what you find.

publicBuild.title: Your build, at its own address
publicBuild.body: Switch a vehicle to public and it gets a readable URL anyone can open — the jobs, the photos and the progress, with the costs left out unless you want them shown.

feed.title: What everyone else is building
feed.body: A feed of published builds, restorations and daily drivers, filtered by mode and searchable. Follow one and you hear about it by email or push when it moves.

partsWanted.title: Ask for the part
partsWanted.body: Post what you can’t find and where you are, and let the rest of the board answer. Posting needs Personal; replying to somebody else’s is free for everyone.

roadmap.title: The list we work from
roadmap.body: Feature requests and bug reports in the open, with votes. Reading it needs no account, and the status on each one is ours to set rather than the author’s.

languages.title: Romanian and English
languages.body: The whole interface, the emails and the PDFs, in both. Switch it at the top of any page: the choice sticks to the browser, while your emails follow your account.

install.title: Installs like an app
install.body: Add it to the home screen and it opens full screen, without a browser bar. It is still the same site, so there is nothing to update.

theme.title: Light and dark
theme.body: A dark theme that was designed rather than inverted, and a system setting that follows your phone. The preference stays on the device.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard, if you prefer
shortcuts.body: g then d for the garage, n for a new job, ? for the list. They are ignored while you are typing in a field, which is why you can have them at all.

yourData.title: Your data, on request
yourData.body: Download everything RigLog holds about you as JSON, or delete the account and take the photos with it. Both are buttons in settings, not an email to support.

free.a: Yes. A free account covers one vehicle, with unlimited jobs, photos, documents and reminders. Personal is {price} RON a month and adds more vehicles, spend analysis, PDF export and the rest. No card is asked for to start, and nothing expires.

phone.q: Does it work on a phone?
phone.a: Yes. It is a web app built for a phone first, and it installs to the home screen and opens full screen — no app store, and nothing to update. It works on a laptop the same way.

reminders.q: Will it remind me about the inspection and the insurance?
reminders.a: Yes. Enter the expiry date once and RigLog emails you 30 days out, again at 14 and again at 3 — once each, not once per check. Renewing the document re-arms all three.

mechanic.q: Can my mechanic add the work they did?
mechanic.a: Yes, on a single vehicle you invite them to. They can add the jobs they did and nothing else, and one toggle hides every price from them — which matters when the person adding the job is also the person charging for it.

private.a: Yes, until you say otherwise. A vehicle is private until you switch it to public, and even then the costs stay hidden unless you choose to show them. Nothing is shared and nothing is advertised against.

daily.q: Is it only for project cars?
daily.a: No. Daily-driver mode is a plain repair and service log: what was done, when, at what mileage and what it cost. It never asks how far along you are, because a repair log does not finish.

leave.q: What if I want to leave?
leave.a: Download everything RigLog holds about you as JSON, or delete the account and take the photos with it. Both are buttons in settings, not an email to support.

session.purpose: Keeps you logged in. It holds a signed token identifying your account — without it every page would ask you to log in again.
session.duration: 30 days, or until you log out

csrf.purpose: Protects sign-in and sign-out from cross-site request forgery — it stops another site submitting those forms on your behalf.

callbackUrl.purpose: Remembers which page to return you to after logging in.

oauthState.purpose: Set only if you sign in with Google. They tie the response from Google back to the request you started, which is what stops that exchange being hijacked.
oauthState.duration: A few minutes, during sign-in only

locale.purpose: Remembers whether you chose Romanian or English. The server renders the text, so it cannot answer in your language without being told which one. It holds no identifier and nothing is authorised by it.
locale.duration: One year, or until you change it

theme.purpose: Your light/dark/system choice (src/lib/theme.ts). Never sent to the server.

cookieNotice.purpose: Remembers that you have seen the cookie notice, so it stops reappearing.

trailRecording.purpose: A crash-recovery copy of a GPS track while you are recording one, so closing the tab by accident does not lose the run. Cleared once the run is saved.

ocrModel.purpose: The Romanian text-recognition model that reads receipts on your device, kept so it is downloaded only once. It holds no personal data; receipts are read on the device and never sent anywhere to be read.

vercel.name: Vercel
vercel.purpose: Hosting, and Blob storage for uploaded photos, receipts and documents.
vercel.dataShared: Everything the app stores, plus the usual server-log data (IP address, browser user agent, requested URL).

stripe.name: Stripe
stripe.purpose: Payments for RigLog’s paid plans and for donations.
stripe.dataShared: Your email address and the payment details you enter on Stripe’s own checkout page. Card numbers never reach RigLog — we store only Stripe’s customer and subscription identifiers.
stripe.when: Only if you buy a plan or donate.

emailProvider.name: Brevo, or Resend
emailProvider.purpose: Sending transactional email — password resets and the notifications you opted into.
emailProvider.dataShared: Your email address and the contents of that message.
emailProvider.when: Whichever is configured for this deployment.

google.name: Google
google.dataShared: Google tells us your email address and name. We do not receive your Google password.
google.when: Only if you use that sign-in option.

openstreetmap.name: OpenStreetMap
openstreetmap.purpose: Map tiles on the trail log.
openstreetmap.dataShared: Your browser requests map images directly from openstreetmap.org, so it sees your IP address and which part of the map you are looking at.
openstreetmap.when: Only on trail log pages, which are off-road projects only.

unpkg.name: unpkg
unpkg.dataShared: Your IP address, as with any image loaded from another site.
unpkg.when: Only on pages showing a map.

nhtsa.name: NHTSA vPIC (US Department of Transportation)
nhtsa.purpose: Decoding a VIN when the built-in table does not recognise it.
nhtsa.dataShared: The VIN you asked to decode. Nothing identifying you is sent with it.
nhtsa.when: Only when you use the VIN decoder.

pushService.name: Your browser’s push service (Google, Mozilla, Apple, …)
pushService.dataShared: The notification’s contents, sent to the endpoint your browser gave us. Which service that is depends on your browser.
pushService.when: Only if you turn push notifications on.

cloudflare.name: Cloudflare (Turnstile)
cloudflare.purpose: Telling a person apart from a script on the sign-up, log-in and password-reset forms.
cloudflare.dataShared: Your IP address, browser and a token the widget generates. Cloudflare states that Turnstile does not use cookies for tracking and does not profile visitors. Your email address and password are never sent to it.
cloudflare.when: Only on those three forms, and only when the operator has configured Turnstile keys.

yourContent.what: Your account, vehicles, tasks, photos, documents, wishlist, trail logs and collaborator invitations
yourContent.howLong: Until you delete them, or until you delete your account — at which point they are removed immediately, including the uploaded files themselves.

publicPosts.what: Feedback tickets, votes, comments, and parts-wanted posts
publicPosts.howLong: Deleted with your account. They disappear from the public board too.

donations.howLong: Kept after account deletion, with your account detached from them. A payment that happened is an accounting record; what is removed is the link to you.

resetTokens.what: Password reset and email confirmation tokens
resetTokens.howLong: One hour for a reset, 24 hours for a confirmation, then they stop working. Deleted with your account.

rateLimits.what: Rate-limiting counters, which stop brute-force and spam
rateLimits.howLong: At most an hour, after which they are swept away. Depending on what is being limited, the counter’s key contains an email address or an IP address alongside the count.

othersWork.rule: Upload someone else’s photos, documents or writing as your own
othersWork.because: Public build pages are indexed by search engines, so this puts their work on the open web under your name.

privateInfo.rule: Post another person’s private information — an address, a phone number, a plate, a VIN that isn’t yours
privateInfo.because: A public project page is public to everyone, permanently, and you cannot un-publish something a search engine has already copied.

spam.rule: Use the feedback board or parts-wanted board for advertising, spam or abuse
spam.because: Both are public and unmoderated by default; they only work if they stay readable.

otherAccounts.rule: Try to reach another account’s vehicles, files or settings
otherAccounts.because: Every route checks ownership, so this is an attempt to break the app rather than a mistake — and it is also a criminal offence.

automation.rule: Automate sign-ups, logins, posts or exports at volume
automation.because: The rate limits exist to keep the free tier affordable; working around them takes the service away from other people.

resale.rule: Resell access, or share one account between several people
resale.because: Personal is priced per person. Collaborator invitations are the supported way to let someone else work on your vehicle.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.whyNoBannerHeading: Why there is no consent banner
cookies.whyNoBanner: RigLog sets {count} kinds of cookie and every one of them is needed for the app to work: staying logged in, protecting the sign-in form, and knowing which language to answer you in. There are no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies, and no third-party scripts that set any.
cookies.exemption: Cookies that are strictly necessary to provide a service you asked for are exempt from the consent requirement in the ePrivacy Directive — but they still have to be disclosed, which is what this page is for. If that ever changes and a cookie is added that isn’t strictly necessary, this page will say so and you will be asked first.
cookies.warning: Some cookies listed below are not strictly necessary. This page needs updating and a consent flow adding before that cookie ships.
cookies.storageHeading: Stored in your browser, but not cookies
cookies.storageIntro: A few things are kept in your browser’s local storage instead. They stay on your device, are never sent to the server, and are gone if you clear site data.
cookies.turningOff: Every browser lets you block or delete cookies. Blocking the ones above will log you out and stop you logging back in — the session cookie is the login. There is no way around that short of not having accounts.
cookies.publicPages: Reading the public pages — this one, the <home>homepage</home>, the <tickets>feedback board</tickets> and public build pages — needs no cookies at all.
cookies.morePrivacy: More about what RigLog stores is in the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

privacy.metaDescription: What RigLog stores, who it is shared with, and how to get a copy or have it deleted.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.shortBody: RigLog stores what you put into it — your vehicles, the work you log, your photos and documents — plus the email address you signed up with. There is no advertising, no tracking, and no analytics script of any kind. Nothing is sold, and nothing is shared except with the services listed below that are needed to run the app.
privacy.shortRights: You can download everything we hold, or delete all of it, from <settings>Profile & settings</settings>. Neither needs you to ask anyone.
privacy.controllerFallback: The operator of this RigLog installation
privacy.controllerLine: {controller} is the data controller for the information described here.
privacy.contactWithEmail: For anything in this policy, including a data request, write to <email></email>.
privacy.contactNoEmail: For anything in this policy, open a ticket on the <tickets>feedback board</tickets>. You do not need to wait for a reply to exercise the rights below — the export and deletion buttons in your settings do both immediately.
privacy.collectAccount: Email address, display name, and a public username generated from that name. Optionally a location and an avatar. We need the email to log you in and to send password resets. Passwords are stored only as a bcrypt hash — nobody, including us, can read them back.
privacy.collectLogged: Vehicles, tasks, costs, photos, receipts, documents and their expiry dates, wishlist items, and GPS tracks if you use the trail log. This is the app’s purpose; it is stored because you asked it to be.
privacy.collectPublic: Feedback tickets, votes and comments, parts-wanted posts, and any project you switch to public. These are visible to anyone, including people without an account, and public projects are indexed by search engines. That is the point of them — but it is worth being deliberate about it.
privacy.collectLogs: Ordinary web-server logs, and short-lived counters used to stop brute-force login attempts and spam. Details are in the retention table below.
privacy.noSpecialCategory: We do not ask for, and have no use for, anything in the “special category” sense — health, politics, beliefs, biometrics. Please don’t put it in a task note.
privacy.basisHeading: Why we are allowed to (legal basis)
privacy.basisContract: your account and everything you log. You asked for an app that remembers your build; it cannot do that without storing it.
privacy.basisInterests: keeping the service secure and working: rate limiting, abuse prevention, server logs.
privacy.basisConsent: optional email and push notifications about projects you follow. You turn them on, and you can turn them off in settings at any time.
privacy.sharingIntro: Only the services needed to run the app. Each one gets the minimum that its job requires, and none of them is an advertising network.
privacy.transfers: Some of these are based outside the EU. Where that is the case, the transfer relies on the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses or an adequacy decision, through the provider’s own data processing terms.
privacy.compelled: We would also hand over data if legally compelled to — a court order, for example. That is not a loophole we go looking for.
privacy.collaborators: If you invite a mechanic or specialist to a vehicle, they can see that vehicle and its tasks, and add work of their own. They cannot see your other vehicles, your account settings, or anything else. You can hide cost totals from them with a setting on the vehicle, and you can revoke an invitation at any time. Revoking removes their access immediately.
privacy.rightAccess: of everything we hold — the Download my data button in settings produces it immediately, as JSON.
privacy.rightRectify: anything wrong — edit it in the app.
privacy.rightErase: the Delete account button in settings removes your account, every project, and the uploaded files themselves. It is immediate and cannot be undone.
privacy.rightPort: the same export is structured JSON, meant to be read by something other than us.
privacy.rightObjectTerm: Object, or ask us to restrict processing
privacy.rightObject: and withdraw consent for notifications at any time.
privacy.rightComplain: to a supervisory authority. In Romania that is <anspdcp>ANSPDCP</anspdcp>; elsewhere in the EU, your own country’s authority.
privacy.rightsButtons: The first two and the middle two are buttons rather than requests on purpose. You should not have to ask permission to leave.
privacy.cookies: RigLog sets only the cookies needed to keep you logged in, to protect the sign-in form, and to remember which language you chose. There are no tracking or advertising cookies, which is why you are not asked to consent to any. <list>The full list is here</list>.
privacy.children: RigLog is not aimed at children and we do not knowingly hold data about anyone under 16. If you believe we do, tell us and it will be removed.
privacy.changes: If this policy changes in substance, the date at the top changes with it. Material changes will be announced on the <tickets>feedback board</tickets> rather than made quietly.

terms.metaDescription: The agreement between you and RigLog: what you get, what you owe, and how either side ends it.
terms.title: Terms of service
terms.short1: RigLog logs the work you do on your vehicles. You own what you put in and can take it out or delete it at any time. One vehicle is free forever; the paid plans cost money and can be cancelled. Don’t post other people’s private information, and don’t try to break the app. If we get something wrong, tell us.
terms.short2: The rest of this page is the same thing in the detail that matters when something goes wrong.
terms.operatorFallback: the operator of this RigLog installation
terms.parties: These terms are between you and {operator} (“we”, “us”). They apply from the moment you create an account.
terms.accountAge: You need to be at least 16 to have an account.
terms.accountEmail: Give a real email address — it is the only way to reset your password, and we can’t recover an account without it.
terms.accountPassword: Keep your password to yourself. Anything done from your account is treated as done by you.
terms.accountOnePerPerson: One account per person. If someone else needs to work on your vehicle, invite them as a collaborator rather than sharing a login.
terms.free: {vehicles} vehicle, unlimited tasks on it, up to {photos} photos per task, documents and reminders, the job-report PDF, collaborators, and your data export. Free means free — there is no trial that quietly ends.
terms.pro: Up to {vehicles} vehicles, unlimited photos, the full cost analytics, PDF build history, shareable cards, the VIN decoder, trail logs and price alerts. {monthly} RON monthly, {annual} RON annually, or {lifetime} RON once for lifetime access.
terms.uploadCap: Uploads are capped at {mb}MB per file on every tier — a platform limit, not a paywall.
terms.tierChanges: We may change what each tier includes. If a change removes something you are paying for, we will say so before it happens and you can cancel and claim a proportional refund for time you have paid for and not used.
terms.paying1: Payments are handled by Stripe. We never see or store your card details — only Stripe’s reference for your customer record.
terms.paying2: Monthly and annual plans renew automatically until you cancel. Cancel any time from <settings>Profile & settings</settings>, which opens Stripe’s billing portal. Cancelling stops the next charge; you keep your plan until the period you have already paid for runs out. Lifetime is a single payment with nothing to cancel.
terms.withdrawal: You can cancel for a full refund within {days} days of buying, for any reason or none. EU and Romanian law give you that right on anything bought at a distance. It can be waived for digital content delivered immediately, but only if you are asked to waive it first — and we don’t ask, so it stands. Email us, or open a ticket, and say you are withdrawing.
terms.afterWithdrawal: After {days} days we don’t give refunds for a change of mind. We do refund when we have charged you in error or the service has been unusable for a meaningful stretch — ask.
terms.losingPro: Losing a paid plan never deletes anything. Your vehicles, photos and history stay exactly where they are; the paid-only screens stop opening, and your export keeps working so you can take everything with you. If you then have more vehicles than your plan covers, the oldest stay editable and the rest become read-only — you can still open, export, unpublish or delete them — until you choose a plan again or remove others.
terms.founding1: The first {limit} accounts ever created get Personal at no charge. If you are one of them, your settings page says so and gives your number.
terms.founding2: It is a gift rather than a purchase: nothing was paid, so there is nothing to refund and no subscription to cancel. It is tied to your account and cannot be transferred or sold.
terms.founding3: “For life” means for as long as RigLog runs. We will not put it behind a payment later, and buying — then cancelling — a paid plan will not remove it. We can withdraw it if the account breaks the rules above, on the same terms as any other account. If RigLog shuts down, it ends with the service; your export still works, and we would give notice.
terms.donations: A donation is a gift toward running costs. It buys nothing, unlocks nothing, and is not refundable — so please only give what you are happy to part with. If you meant to buy a plan and donated by mistake, tell us and we will sort it out.
terms.content1: Your photos, notes, receipts and build history belong to you. We claim no ownership of them.
terms.content2: To run the service we need your permission to store your content, back it up, and show it back to you and to anyone you have given access — collaborators you invite, and the whole internet for a project you switch to public. That permission covers nothing else: we do not sell it, license it on, use it to advertise, or train anything on it. It ends when you delete the content or your account.
terms.content3: Public is properly public. A public project page, a feedback ticket and a parts-wanted post are visible to everyone and are indexed by search engines. Making a project private again stops us serving it, but we cannot make a search engine forget a copy it has already taken. Decide accordingly before you publish a plate, a VIN or a driveway.
terms.mustNotIntro: Each of these maps to something the app actually exposes:
terms.collaborators1: Inviting someone gives them access to that vehicle and its tasks, and lets them add work of their own. They cannot see your other vehicles or your account settings. You choose who to invite and can revoke access at any time, which takes effect immediately.
terms.collaborators2: Work a collaborator logs on your vehicle stays in your history if they later delete their account — their name comes off it, the record does not.
terms.promiseHeading: What we promise, and what we don’t
terms.promise1: We will run the service with reasonable care and skill, and tell you about planned downtime where we can.
terms.promise2: We do not promise it will never be down, never lose a request, or never have a bug. Treat RigLog as a convenient copy of your records, not the only one: an export button sits in your settings for exactly that reason, and if a vehicle’s history matters to a sale or an insurance claim, keep your own copy.
terms.promise3: The VIN decoder, originality score, cost analytics and reminders are aids, not professional advice. Check an expiry date against the document itself before you rely on it.
terms.liability1: Nothing here limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for anything else the law says cannot be limited — including your rights as a consumer, which these terms do not reduce.
terms.liability2: Beyond that, our liability for any claim is capped at what you have paid us in the 12 months before it arose, and we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss — missed sales, lost profits, or the value of data you did not keep a copy of.
terms.endingYou: Delete your account from settings. It removes your data immediately, including the uploaded files themselves. It cannot be undone, so take your export first if you want one.
terms.endingUs: We can suspend or close an account that breaks the rules above, or that puts the service or other people at risk. Where it is reasonable to do so we will warn you first and give you a chance to fix it, and we will tell you why. If we close a paid account for a reason that isn’t your breach, we refund the unused part of what you have paid.
terms.changes: The date at the top changes whenever the substance does. For a change that materially affects you we will announce it on the <tickets>feedback board</tickets> before it takes effect, rather than editing this page quietly. Carrying on using the account after that is acceptance; if you would rather not, delete the account and, if you are on a paid plan, ask for the unused part back.
terms.law1: Romanian law applies, and the courts of Romania have jurisdiction. If you are a consumer resident elsewhere in the EU, this does not deprive you of the protection of your own country’s mandatory consumer law, nor of the right to bring a claim there.
terms.law2: Please raise a problem with us first — most things are a misunderstanding and get fixed the same week. If that fails you can go to <authority></authority>, or use the EU’s <odr>online dispute resolution platform</odr>.
terms.law3: How we handle your personal data is in the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>, which is part of this agreement.

admin.diagnosticsBroken: Something here is broken, and people using the site are hitting it.

admin.triageNotePlaceholder: Optional note shown publicly on the ticket…
admin.reportedVersion: Version reported by the reporter's browser
admin.organizationsIntro: Every organisation in the closed beta: who owns it and how big it is. Read-only — being an admin gives no access to a company’s vehicles or records.

admin.orgBetaNone: No account has it switched on yet.

verifyEmail.bannerBody: Until {email} is confirmed, this account cannot publish a build, invite a mechanic, or post in the community. The link is in the confirmation email — or send another.
verifyEmail.resent: Sent. Check your inbox — and your spam folder, since it is the first message we have sent you.
verifyEmail.resendFailed: That did not send. Either the address cannot receive mail, or this deployment has no mail provider set up.
verifyEmail.resendRateLimited: Too many requests. Try again in about {minutes, plural, one {a minute} other {# minutes}}.
verifyEmail.unverifiedHelp: Confirming proves the address is yours. Until then your garage works normally — what is held back is everything that reaches other people: publishing a build, inviting a mechanic, and posting on the feedback and parts boards.
verifyEmail.notEnforced: This deployment cannot send email, so nothing is being held back and no link can be sent. Set a mail provider to switch confirmation back on — see /admin/diagnostics.
verifyEmail.successBody: Your address is confirmed. Everything in RigLog is open to you.
verifyEmail.alreadyBody: This address was already confirmed — you may have opened the link twice. Nothing more to do.
verifyEmail.expiredBody: Confirmation links last 24 hours. Log in and send yourself a new one from Settings.
verifyEmail.invalidBody: Some mail apps break a long link across two lines. Copy the whole link out of the email, or log in and send a new one from Settings.
verifyEmail.missingBody: It arrived without its token. Copy the whole link from the email, or log in and send a new one from Settings.
verifyEmail.nothingToSend: This address is already confirmed — there is nothing to send.

version.settingsHelp: The build running in this browser. Tap to copy it — including it in a bug report is the fastest way to tell whether a fix has reached you.
version.unknownHelp: This build carries no version information, which happens when it was built outside the normal deploy. Nothing is wrong with the app.

vehicleProfile.plateHelp: Only you and your collaborators see it. It never appears on the public page.

odometer.distance: {km} km logged since the first reading

odometer.taskKmHelp: What the odometer read when the job was done. It goes into the vehicle’s mileage history.
odometer.why: Readings stay in date order: each one must sit between the ones before and after it.

fuel.notYet: Consumption appears after two full tanks with the odometer recorded at each.

vehicleValues.currentValueRon: What you think it's worth now (RON)
vehicleValues.currentValueHelp: Your own estimate. RigLog never suggests a value, because it has no data to base one on.
vehicleValues.currentValueHelpDated: Your own estimate, last changed on {date}. RigLog never suggests a value.

vehicleValues.leasingHelp: Monthly payments count towards the cost of ownership.

coverage.documentsWithoutPrice: {count, plural, one {# document has} other {# documents have}} no price.

coverage.financeIncomplete: Finance is set, but without a monthly payment or first payment date, so no payments are counted.

passport.what: The owner's own records, kept in RigLog. It is not a vehicle history report, a registry check or an inspection: RigLog stores what the owner entered and verifies none of it.
passport.snapshot: Snapshot generated on {date}. The shared link may have changed since.
passport.missingTitle: What these records do not cover

absence.noJobs: No completed jobs recorded in RigLog.
absence.noMileage: No odometer readings recorded in RigLog.
absence.noAccidentsRecorded: Accidents and damage: none recorded in RigLog. That is not the same as none having happened.

passport.kmRestarts: km restarts after an odometer replacement
passport.documentsNote: As entered by the owner, not checked against any registry.

passport.withdrawn: Link withdrawn. It no longer opens.
passport.linkReplaced: New link created. The old one no longer opens.

passport.pdfHelp: The PDF is a dated snapshot with the same choices as the link.
passport.ownerViewAdvice: Every section below is the owner’s own account, as they entered it. Before relying on it, compare it with receipts, an independent inspection and the official registry.

organizations.title: Organisations
organizations.intro: A company account: its vehicles, its members and what each of them may do.
organizations.none: You don’t belong to any organisation.
organizations.createHelp: You become its first owner. The fiscal code is optional and can be added later. It holds vehicles once it has a plan, chosen on its billing page.
organizations.betaNote: Organisations are in a closed beta. Ask us to switch them on for your account.
organizations.settingsHelp: Company accounts you belong to, and the people in them.
organizations.name: Company name
organizations.cuiHelp: With or without RO. The check digit is verified; the registry is not consulted.
organizations.rolesHelp: Owners run the organisation: its details, its members and deleting it. Owners and fleet managers manage its vehicles like their own; mechanics and drivers see them and log their own work. There is always at least one owner.
organizations.confirmLeave: Leave this organisation? You will need a new invitation to come back.
organizations.deleteHelp: Deletes the organisation and every membership in it. People’s own accounts and personal vehicles are not touched.
organizations.confirmDelete: Delete {name} and every membership in it? This cannot be undone.
organizations.inviteHelp: They get an email with a link that lasts 7 days, and must log in with this address to accept it.
organizations.confirmWithdraw: Withdraw the invitation to {email}? Its link will stop working.

accept.missingToken: This invitation link is missing its token.
accept.invited: You’ve been invited to join an organisation on RigLog. Log in or create an account with the email address the invitation was sent to, then come back to this link.
accept.accepted: You’re in. You are now a member of the organisation.

organizations.vehiclesHelp: Move a vehicle in, or out to your own garage, from its settings page. Everyone here can see these.
organizations.noVehicles: No vehicles yet. The owner of a personal vehicle can move it in from the vehicle’s settings.

move.title: Move to an organisation
move.help: The vehicle becomes the company’s: its owners and fleet managers manage it, its mechanics and drivers see it and log their work. You keep access through your role there. An owner or fleet manager can move it back out to their own garage.
move.unpublishes: This vehicle is public. A company vehicle can’t be, so moving it makes it private.
move.confirm: Move this vehicle to {name}? Who can see it will be decided by the roles there.

organizations.deleteVehiclesWarning: This also deletes its {count, plural, one {# vehicle} other {# vehicles}} with every job, photo, document and file. To keep one, move it to your garage from its settings first.

moveOut.title: Move to my garage
moveOut.help: Takes this vehicle out of {name} and makes it one of your personal vehicles. Nobody in the organisation will see it any more, apart from collaborators you invited to it directly.
moveOut.confirm: Take this vehicle out of {name} and into your own garage? Its members lose access to it.
moveOut.moved: The vehicle is now in your garage.

fleet.title: Fleet compliance
fleet.intro: Every vehicle against every document a roadside check asks for, with the days left on each. Vehicles with anything expired come first.
fleet.missing: No ITP or RCA on record
fleet.caption: Documents per vehicle, days until each expires
fleet.footnote: Days come from the expiry dates entered on each vehicle, the same count the reminder emails use. “None recorded” means RigLog has no record, not that the vehicle has none. Historic status is shown but changes nothing here.

cost.title: Fleet cost
cost.intro: What the fleet costs to run, from each vehicle’s own cost-of-ownership record. Nothing is estimated: a vehicle whose record has gaps is marked, and its page lists them.
cost.caption: Cost per vehicle in the period
cost.noCosts: No costs recorded in this period.
cost.footnote: Running cost leaves out the purchase price, which isn’t a monthly cost. Per vehicle per month divides the running cost by the months each vehicle was owned in the period. Each vehicle’s figures are the ones on its own costs page.

drivers.title: Drivers
drivers.intro: Who drives this vehicle now, and who has before. A driver sees only the vehicle assigned to them — its log, photos and documents — and never its costs.
drivers.none: No one is assigned to this vehicle.
drivers.noDrivers: This organisation has no members with the driver role. Invite one from the organisation page.
drivers.confirmEnd: End {name}’s assignment now? They lose access to this vehicle straight away.
drivers.noHistory: Nobody has been assigned to this vehicle yet.
drivers.startKmHelp: If you know it. Otherwise the driver records it when they take the vehicle.

defect.title: Report a defect
defect.intro: Something wrong with the vehicle? Say what, add a photo, and it goes on its log as a job that needs attention — the fleet manager sees it on their garage.
defect.photoFailed: The report was saved, but the photo could not be added.

handover.photosChosen: {count, plural, one {# photo chosen} other {# photos chosen}}
handover.photoFailed: A photo could not be uploaded; nothing else was saved.
handover.confirmEnd: Hand the vehicle back now? You lose access to it straight away.

driverPanel.title: You’re driving this vehicle

driverPanel.endHelp: The odometer and condition photos as you hand it back. Photos are saved first; ending the assignment removes your access.

invoiceScan.failed: Couldn't read this invoice. Type the job in — the photo will still be attached.
invoiceScan.attachFailed: The job was saved, but the invoice couldn't be attached.
invoiceScan.pro: Scan workshop invoices instead of typing them — with Personal
invoiceScan.unsure: Couldn't read this clearly — type it from the invoice.
invoiceScan.unsureDate: Couldn't read the date clearly — check it against the invoice.

invoiceScan.noSplitWithTotal: The invoice lines didn't add up to its total ({total} lei), so parts and labour weren't filled in — type them from the invoice.

fleetReport.title: Fleet reports

fleetReport.limit: Up to {days} days at a time.

error.reportPeriodInvalid: Choose a start day on or before the end day.
error.reportPeriodTooLong: A report covers at most {days} days. Split the period in two.

files.summaryHelp: Spend per vehicle, with who drove it, and per category; the documents that expired or were renewed.
files.jobsHelp: Every job in the period: vehicle, registration, category, parts, labour, workshop, and who logged it.
files.costsHelp: Every cost — jobs, fuel, documents, tyres, expenses, finance — with the driver assigned that day.

outcome.newerOnRecord: A newer one of this type is on record

trips.introDriver: Your trips on this vehicle, business or personal, with the km at each end. You see and export only your own.

trips.pro: On a personal vehicle the trip sheet comes with Personal. On a company vehicle it comes with the organisation.

csv.withoutDistance: Trips without a distance (a reading was deleted)

plans.annualNote: Each also by the year, for the price of ten months.
plans.companyIntroOpen: Several users, drivers, fleet compliance, reports and trip sheets — bought by an organisation, with its own card and invoices.

The oldest vehicles stay editable; to edit this one again, choose a plan that covers it, delete another vehicle, or move one into an organisation.

readOnly.companyBody: The organisation’s plan does not cover this vehicle right now, so nothing can be added or changed here. Everything recorded is still here.

orgBilling.noPlan: No plan yet. The organisation can invite people, but holds vehicles only on a plan.

orgBilling.paymentFailedOwner: The last payment failed. Everything keeps working while Stripe retries — update the card from Plan and billing so the plan does not end.
orgBilling.readOnlyCount: {count, plural, one {# vehicle is} other {# vehicles are}} read-only: the plan covers fewer than the organisation holds. Nothing was hidden or deleted — a plan that covers them makes them editable again, or move some out.
orgBilling.manageHelp: Change the plan, update the card, download invoices or cancel — in Stripe’s billing portal. Cancelling keeps every vehicle, read-only.
orgBilling.chooseHelp: Billed to the organisation. If it ever holds more vehicles than its plan covers, the newest ones become read-only until the plan covers them — never hidden or deleted.
orgBilling.notConfigured: Company plans are not on sale yet.
orgBilling.subscribed: Thank you. The plan shows here as soon as Stripe confirms the payment, usually within a minute.
orgBilling.invoicesHelp: Past invoices and the card on file are in Stripe’s billing portal.
